questions.stem: Rice at ₹30/kg and ₹45/kg is mixed to sell at ₹36/kg. The mixing ratio is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 1 — alligation. Cheaper:Dearer = (45 − 36) : (36 − 30) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2. Verify: 3×30 + 2×45 = 90+90 = 180 over 5 kg → 36/kg. ✓
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: 40 L of milk has 10 L replaced with water. This is repeated once more. The milk percentage finally is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 2 — repeated replacement. Final pure = Initial × (1 − x/V)^n = 40 × (3/4)^2 = 22.5 L → 22.5/40 = 56.25%. Distractor 75% = (3/4) once only.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two alloys contain silver and copper in ratios 3:2 and 5:3. Equal weights of each are melted together. The new ratio of silver to copper is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 3 — combine two mixtures. Take 1 kg of each. From A: 3/5 Ag + 2/5 Cu. From B: 5/8 Ag + 3/8 Cu. Sum Ag = 3/5 + 5/8 = 24/40 + 25/40 = 49/40. Cu = 2/5 + 3/8 = 16/40 + 15/40 = 31/40. Ratio 49:31.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: In what ratio must tea at ₹100/kg be mixed with tea at ₹160/kg so that the mixture costs ₹120/kg?
questions.explanation: TYPE 1 — alligation. (160 − 120) : (120 − 100) = 40 : 20 = 2:1 (cheaper : dearer). So 2 parts of ₹100 tea to 1 part of ₹160 tea.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: 30 L of a mixture has 20% alcohol. Water is added to make alcohol 15%. Water added equals:
questions.explanation: Pure alcohol stays = 20% of 30 = 6 L. After adding x L, 6/(30+x) = 15/100 → 30+x = 40 → x = 10 L.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A mixture of 60 L has milk and water in 2:1. Water added to make the ratio 1:2 is:
questions.explanation: Milk = 40 L, water = 20 L. To reach milk:water = 1:2, water must become 80 L. Add 80 − 20 = 60 L.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A vessel contains 50 L milk. 5 L is drawn and replaced with water. This is done thrice. Milk remaining is:
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A dishonest milkman sells a mixture of milk and water for the price of pure milk. If his profit is 25%, the ratio of water to milk is:
questions.explanation: Water is free (CP = 0). For 25% profit, he must add water so that every 5 L sold contains 4 L milk + 1 L water. Water:Milk = 1:4.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
